title: Singulate the middle box from a tightly packed 3 x 3 cluster and put it on the pad
instruction: Put the blue box from the middle of the cluster on the green pad. Keep the other eight boxes on the grey mat the whole time, each sitting flat on the mat, not on another box.
context: Order pickers and piece-picking robots with finger grippers often face items packed side to side (a suction cup could lift one from above; fingers cannot). No single push frees the middle item: room has to be made by moving its neighbours, and they must stay on the mat.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases (which are 61 cm apart). Grey mat (fixed, grey rubber sheet taped to the table): 310 mm front to back and 320 mm wide, 2 mm thick, spanning 12.0 to 43.0 cm in front of the arm bases and from 4.0 cm right of the midline to 28.0 cm left of it. Cubes (loose): nine cardboard boxes, each a 50 mm cube of 60 g, sitting on the mat in a 3 x 3 square with their sides square to the table, packed side to side (0.2 mm between neighbours, so no finger fits between them). The square's centre cube is blue and stands 32.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 17.0 cm left of the midline; the other eight are brown and stand at 50.2 mm pitch around it, so the square spans 24.5 to 39.5 cm in front and 9.5 to 24.5 cm left of the midline. Green pad (fixed, green card taped to the table): 80 x 80 mm, 2 mm thick, centred 20.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 34.5 cm left of the midline (20 cm in front of the left arm's base and 4 cm to its left), 25 mm beyond the mat's left edge. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Every stated limit is inclusive. A cube is at rest when it moves less than 1 cm/s and turns less than 0.5 rad/s. A cube lies flat when its highest point is at most 53 mm above its lowest (about 3.4 degrees of tilt). A brown cube is on the mat when it lies flat, its bottom is within 3 mm of the mat's top, and its centre is over the mat. The brown cubes are intact when, for the whole trial, no brown cube's centre has passed beyond the mat's edge (a cube pushed or carried off and put back still counts, even if put back exactly in its starting place), and at the end all eight are on the mat and at rest. The scorer's record of the trial is cleared only by an episode reset, which it recognises as every cube within 0.5 mm of its starting place and at rest, reached by a jump of more than 50 mm since the previous control step. Finger room: a 15 mm deep strip laid against the whole of each of two opposite side faces of the blue cube overlaps no other cube (touching its outer edge is allowed). Score 1.0: the blue cube lies flat on the green pad, its bottom within 1 mm of the pad's top, wholly inside the pad's edges, at rest, and the brown cubes are intact. Score 0.5: the blue cube's centre is off the mat and it lies flat and at rest with its bottom within 1 mm of the table, or with its centre over the pad and its bottom within 1 mm of the pad's top (on the pad but over its edge), and the brown cubes are intact. Score 0.25: the blue cube lies flat on the mat with its bottom within 1 mm of the mat's top and its centre over the mat, at rest, with finger room, and the brown cubes are intact. Score 0 in every other case, including the blue cube held above any surface, still moving, tilted or on top of another cube, and any brown cube ever off the mat, left on another cube, leaning or still moving. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Set the nine cubes back in the packed 3 x 3 square at the positions above, blue in the middle, sides square to the table. Nothing is consumed. Runs use object_jitter=0, which this task needs: jitter would break the packed square.
fidelity: Approximate. Boxes are rigid cubes with the simulator's friction, not cardboard that crushes or bends; real cartons vary in size, so real packed clusters have uneven gaps. The mat and pad are fixed thin boxes. The 0.2 mm gaps stand in for touching boxes. Mass and friction are not measured from real boxes.
